overview: Sigma 4.11's ChestStealer drains chests one item at a time through the vanilla container protocol. Every steal passes through mc.playerController.windowClick, which emits C0EPacketClickWindow against the open window id, paced by a timer of 50 milliseconds per delay-setting tick. The Hypixel mode doubles every steal into two shift-clicks (button 0 then button 1) so each item costs two C0E packets, and the Drop option appends a -999 outside-window throw. A title blacklist refuses to touch shop, selector and lobby GUIs, the item filter keeps junk and worse swords out of the inventory, and the optional ChestAura opens nearby chests with C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement sent through the no-event packet path. The module closes the chest with the client closeScreen once the viewed contents are gone or the inventory is full.

sections.p: The handler runs on EventUpdate pre. While a GuiChest is open and the title passes the blacklist, a per-item delay is computed as 50 times the Delay setting (default 2, so 100ms per item) and gated through a Sigma Timer. A First Delay setting (default 0, range 0 to 15) holds the first click for that many update ticks. Each steal is a windowClick against the chest window id, and the timer resets after every click. The loop first verifies the player inventory is not full, then scans the chest slots for the first stack that passes the isBad filter; when nothing stealable remains, or when the inventory is full, the module closes the screen and clears the stealing flag.

In Hypixel mode each item costs two window clicks: the first with button 0 and the second with button 1, both in shift mode, which doubles the C0E rate to roughly 20 packets per second at the default delay. With Drop enabled the steal is a left-click pickup followed by a -999 outside-window throw, and the server-side drop is also issued per item. The isBad filter compares candidate swords against the best sword already in the inventory using sharpness times 1.25 plus base damage, and rejects a long unlocalized-name list (tnt, sticks, eggs, string, flint, compass, feathers, buckets, snow, fish, enchantments, xp, shears, anvils, torches, seeds, leather, pistons), plus pickaxes, glass bottles, tools and harmful splash potions. The chest-title blacklist holds about forty substrings such as menu, selector, game, shop, lobby, vault and anticheat, and any match makes the handler return without stealing.

ChestAura is a separate pre-update branch that runs while no screen is open. It walks the loaded tile-entity list, and for each TileEntityChest within 4 blocks that is not marked empty it sends a C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the chest position, a ray-traced facing direction and the current held item through NetUtil.sendPacketNoEvents, then marks the chest empty client-side and breaks. The stealTimer gates re-scans at 1000ms and resets the stealing flag after 2000ms of inactivity, so the module re-opens chests as they become available. The C08 goes out through the network manager's no-event path, bypassing the client's outgoing event bus.

files.label: ChestStealer.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is one EventUpdate handler with two branches. The chest branch runs the paced steal loop: it computes the 50-millisecond per-item delay, applies the first-delay counter, verifies the inventory is not full, scans for a non-bad stack and shift-clicks it through windowClick, which emits C0E via the fork's PlayerControllerMP. The Hypixel double-click and the Drop throw are extra windowClick calls in the same branch. The ChestAura branch opens nearby chests with C08 through NetUtil.sendPacketNoEvents and tracks them with a client-side isEmpty flag.\n\nThe close path is mc.thePlayer.closeScreen, which the Sigma fork's EntityPlayerSP overrides to queue C0DPacketCloseWindow with the open container window id. The C09 held-item chip is inherited from the client's window protocol: the fork's windowClick emits pure C0E and only other sync paths, like the per-tick updateController sync, ever emit C09, and this module never changes the held item. The title blacklist and the sword-damage comparison are pure client-side filters that decide which stacks are worth a click.

files.label: NetUtil.java (no-event send path)
files.explanation: NetUtil is the module's only external helper. sendPacketNoEvents routes a packet straight to the network manager's sendPacketNoEvent, which queues it for the wire without running it through the client's outgoing event bus, so no other module or event listener can cancel or observe the ChestAura open in flight. sendPacket sends through the normal event-visible path. The module uses the no-event variant specifically for the C08 chest-open packets so the open cannot be intercepted by other handlers.\n\nThe distinction matters for the wire behavior: both paths ultimately reach the server, and the server sees the C08 as a normal use-item-on-block action that opens the chest and starts the S30 window refresh the steal loop then consumes. The class is a thin static wrapper over the fork's NetworkManager, which is why it is the right supporting file for the ChestAura half of the module.

countering.label: FastClick (window click rate)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus FastClick scores InventoryClickEvent traffic into an ActionFrequency with five 200ms buckets: the newest bucket is compared against the short-term limit of 4 and the full window against the normal limit of 15, with TickTask lag division before the comparison. A plain shift-click with an empty cursor counts 1.0 via getAmountWithAction. The check also carries the container-interaction path: any click landing within the 155ms min-interaction-duration default after the container opened adds a violation of (155 / duration) * 100. Slot -999 outside-window throws are excluded entirely, so the Drop mode's throws never count.\n\nThe stock Sigma configuration sits just under the rate limits: 100ms per item is 10 clicks per second, or 2 per bucket, below both the short-term 4 and the window 15, so a default-delay drain passes the rate paths. Hypixel mode changes that: two clicks per item at 20 per second blows the 15 window (roughly 5 VL per click, cancel at vl>150 in about 1.5 seconds) and touches the 4-per-bucket short-term limit. The interact_time path is the most reliable hit because the First Delay default of 0 lands the first click within a frame of the chest opening, deep inside the 155ms window, worth close to 100 VL on its own. The honest gap is the delay dial: raising Delay to 4 ticks or more puts the rate back under both windows.

countering.label: Open (inventory close on movement)
countering.explanation: NCP's Open check watches PlayerMoveEvent traffic while an inventory window is open. checkOnMove skips duplicate packets, vehicles, creative quickbar clicks, merchants and velocity-affected moves, then decides whether the move carries an impulse: with modern input it reads the WASD/jump bits directly, otherwise it falls back to the movement model's hasImpulse decision. An impulse while open feeds Improbable and returns true, and the caller force-closes the inventory, resetting inventoryOpenTime and containerInteractTime.\n\nThe module does not suppress movement, so any strafing or stepping during a drain is visible to the check and a single impulse move mid-steal closes the chest and aborts the session. The practical tension is that chest stealers stand still by design, so a careful user never trips it; the check still matters because it resets the very timestamps FastClick's interact_time path reads, wiping the open-time baseline the module's instant first click is measured against. ChestAura's own motion, walking between chests, happens while no window is open and is invisible to this check.

countering.label: InventoryActions (window state mismatch)
countering.explanation: Hawk's InventoryActions punishes world interaction while a window is open and, more importantly for stealers, punishes ClickInventoryEvent packets when HawkPlayer.hasInventoryOpen() is zero. Hawk derives the open state from the S2D window-open, C16 inventory command and close packets, so it tracks the same window lifecycle the server sees, not the client's GUI state, and every punish calls e.resync().\n\nThe module's close path is the race surface: mc.thePlayer.closeScreen emits C0D the moment the client-side view looks empty, but if the server-side close is processed later, or if a stale S30 refresh armed the loop for a window Hawk already considers closed, the client can emit a C0E for a window Hawk sees as closed, and that click is punished and resynced. The world-interaction branch is the other edge: ChestAura swings and right-clicks while walking between chests, and any InteractEntity, BlockDig, ArmSwing or InteractWorld event while the window flag is non-zero is punished, so a close that races the next chest open turns into a resync. The check is content-blind and window-id aware, so randomized delays change nothing.

countering.label: FastConsume (eat-duration; silent for stealers)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's FastConsume guards the item-use path of the inventory family. The inventory listener stamps a consume time on the right-click of an edible or potion, and the check compares it against the consume-time limit (1280ms default) when PlayerItemConsumeEvent fires, flagging any consume that completes faster than a real eat could. The mechanism only engages when a consume event actually lands, which requires the full vanilla use duration to elapse.\n\nFor a chest stealer the check is silent by design: shift-click C0E traffic and C08 chest opens never produce a consume event, so FastConsume stays quiet through an entire drain, and the -999 throws are equally invisible to it. The entry belongs in this set because the same C0E corpus pools the eat-rate checks with the click-rate checks, and it documents the boundary honestly: the inventory family's real pressure on this module is FastClick's click ledger, while FastConsume is the guard for the instant-consume sibling modules (AutoSoup and AutoEat), which would trip it on any server that processes eats immediately.
